items.h: Putin meets U.S. envoys; Kremlin says what could be a record prisoner swap is in the works
items.fact: After Russian President Vladimir Putin met U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the Kremlin on November 12, presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks would continue and that the terms of what would likely be the largest prisoner exchange to date are being finalized. Witkoff said, “We’ve set a new meeting.”

items.h: Zelensky says Starshield speed cap is back; SpaceX official says “this is false”
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 12 that the Starshield satellite terminals used by Ukraine’s military are being systematically capped at 161 km/h (100 mph), making Russian jet-powered drones far harder to intercept. A SpaceX official told the U.S. outlet TWZ, “This is false,” and “There has been no change.”

items.h: Trump says the U.S. doesn’t need an Iran deal; on force, “it’s possible I would do it right now”
items.fact: President Donald Trump posted on social media on November 12 (U.S. time): “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.” The same day, asked by a Salem News Channel host what he would do if Iran threatened U.S. allies and ships, he said that if he saw things going the other way he would act, and “it’s possible I would do it right now.”

items.h: CENTCOM dismisses report it advised Israel to prepare for renewed Iran operations
items.fact: Israeli public broadcaster KAN, citing a U.S. official, reported that U.S. Central Command advised Israel to prepare for a possible resumption of military operations against Iran in the near future. In comments to Anadolu Agency published November 13, a CENTCOM official dismissed the account as “pure speculation” and said there had been no change to the U.S. force posture in the region.

items.h: Kremlin points to first-ever three-way summit China is planning in Shenzhen
items.fact: Presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said on November 12 that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump is planned on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and that he hopes the trilateral summit China is organizing there, the first of its kind, will help stabilize the international situation. The Kremlin did not name the three parties; Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on November 10 that a U.S.-China-Russia leaders’ meeting on the APEC sidelines “should be possible” (Reuters).

items.h: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns as CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
items.fact: Nvidia announced on November 12 (U.S. time) that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, and that CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her current role. The company gave no reason, and the board has begun a search for a permanent CEO.

more.t: The ninth European Political Community summit met in Dublin on November 12. Speaking there, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is trying to get details on the Starshield limits from the American side, “but so far, we know very little” (Ukrinform).

items.h: U.S.-brokered Abu Dhabi talks yield a deal in principle on a prisoner swap, no breakthrough
items.fact: Two days of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended November 11 with Ukraine's chief negotiator, foreign intelligence chief Rustem Umerov, and Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky saying the sides had agreed in principle on a large-scale prisoner exchange. There was no major progress toward ending the war, and U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner (President Donald Trump's son-in-law) are set to meet President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on November 12.

items.h: Ghalibaf says Iran and Oman set the rules in Hormuz; Vance reported to weigh meeting Rezaei
items.fact: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told Al Jazeera in an interview published November 11 that the Strait of Hormuz is “governed by the laws of the two littoral states that border it,” Iran and Oman, and repeated that the U.S. must lift its blockade and sanctions, among other conditions, before talks can begin. The same day, The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance was considering a face-to-face meeting with Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, and that the discussions were preliminary.

items.h: Trump says he wants “a total victory, not a 93 percent victory” in Iran, says ending the war is “just a question of when”
items.fact: Speaking at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day, November 11, President Donald Trump said of the Iran war, “We won,” and that it was “just a question of when we want to end it.” He added: “We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93 percent victory.”

items.h: Eisenkot urges Netanyahu in a letter to hold off on “dangerous moves” until a new government is in place
items.fact: Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming Israel's next government, wrote to caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on November 11 urging him to refrain from dangerous moves that can wait until a new government is sworn in. Gulf News, citing Israeli media, reported that Netanyahu had pushed for action against Iran despite objections from IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir, a claim that has not been confirmed.

items.h: Taiwan's defense minister says China ran “area denial drills” in the western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group
items.fact: Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo told reporters at the Legislative Yuan in Taipei on November 10 that China “has indeed conducted area denial drills in the Western Pacific” with the Liaoning carrier group and other formations, Reuters reported. National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu had said that as of November 3 more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels were deployed across the western Pacific. China has not formally announced the drills.

items.h: Indonesian Vice President Gibran hands his resignation to the MPR a day after House factions moved to impeach him
items.fact: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka delivered his resignation to leaders of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) at the parliament complex in Jakarta on the morning of November 12, local time, Antara reported. A day earlier, every faction in the House of Representatives had submitted a motion invoking the House's right to express an opinion, the first step toward impeachment.

more.t: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles shortly after 1 a.m. local time on November 12, hours after the Abu Dhabi talks ended, according to the Kyiv Post.

The Saudi-led coalition said November 11 that it intercepted five missiles and two drones fired by the Houthis toward Riyadh and the kingdom's western and southern regions. Saudi civil defense said debris from ballistic missiles fell on the village of Sabuhah in the Mecca region, Gulf News reported.

Al Jazeera reported November 11 that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed three tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an “unauthorized route” in the eastern Strait of Hormuz; the claim could not be independently verified.

The leaders' segment of the UN climate conference, COP31, opened a two-day run in Antalya, Turkey, on November 11, with more than 70 world leaders and senior officials scheduled to speak, AP reported.

items.h: Rubio says strikes on Iran are unnecessary if economic pressure achieves the same goal; Iran's Rezaei denies talks
items.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Paris on November 10 after a G7 foreign ministers' meeting, said there was no need to strike Iran: “We don't need to conduct military strikes if we're achieving the same objective through economic means and economic pressure.” The same day, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called reports of talks with Washington “complete lies” in a broadcast interview and said the Strait of Hormuz would stay closed until all seven of Iran's conditions were met, according to Anadolu.

items.h: U.S.-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi run about four hours on day one; Rubio says they appear to have been “very productive”
items.fact: Russian and Ukrainian delegations met for about four hours in Abu Dhabi on November 10 in talks mediated by the United States, with a second day set for November 11, the AP reported. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the session constructive and quite substantive and said it covered prisoner exchanges, the return of detained civilians and of children deported from Ukraine, and security guarantees.

items.h: Tanker struck northeast of Lima, Oman; ship attacks around Hormuz hit a wartime monthly high of 37 in October
items.fact: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile in waters northeast of Lima, Oman, on November 10 but did not say who was responsible. Reuters reported that, according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, 37 ships were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October, the most in any month since the war began, and that 10 more attacks had been recorded so far in November.

items.h: Indonesian Vice President Gibran offers his resignation to Prabowo
items.fact: State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said on November 10 that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka had offered his resignation during a meeting of more than two hours with President Prabowo Subianto. It was not disclosed whether Prabowo had accepted it. Gibran has been under pressure since a court found that his educational documents did not meet the eligibility requirements to run in the election.

more.t: Russia launched 163 drones and one Kh-59/69 guided missile at Ukraine between 6 p.m. on November 10 and 8 a.m. on November 11, local time, Ukraine's air force said, adding that 144 drones were shot down or suppressed and 17 locations were hit.
Russia's oil refining capacity has fallen by about 30 percent since late October because of renewed Ukrainian drone attacks, Reuters reported, citing industry sources.

Qatar's Foreign Ministry said at a press briefing in Doha on November 10 that it was receiving positive responses from both Washington and Tehran on a diplomatic solution and that negotiations were making progress, though it could not assess how close a deal was.

items.h: Trump says "Iran militarily is effectively over" after meeting Qatar's prime minister, but keeps blockade
items.fact: President Donald Trump, after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on November 9, said there was momentum toward ending the war but that the naval blockade would remain in place. On Truth Social, he said renewed strikes were quite unlikely. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it fake news about imaginary talks.

items.h: China extends rare earth export control pause to January 10, 2027, and delays other countermeasures
items.fact: China's Commerce Ministry said in a short statement on November 9 that it would extend by two months, to January 10, 2027, its suspension of the export controls on rare earths and other materials that it expanded in October 2025. Reuters reported that the move was part of a wider extension, announced the same day, of China's suspension of trade countermeasures and tariffs.

items.h: U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi, the first since February in Geneva
items.fact: U.S.-brokered three-way talks with Russia and Ukraine were set to resume in Abu Dhabi on November 10, TASS reported. TASS said presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation and that the three sides last met in Geneva on February 18.

items.h: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for supermarket cyberattack, summons envoy
items.fact: Paris prosecutors said on November 9 that Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the October 12 cyberattack that remotely tampered with refrigeration systems in French supermarkets, and sought international arrest warrants for the leaders of the affiliated Shahid Kaveh group. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador was being summoned and that sanctions would be imposed at the European level.

items.h: GOP Rep. Massie files impeachment articles against Hegseth over the Iran war
items.fact: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, on November 9 filed eight articles of impeachment accusing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of, among other things, abusing his powers and illegally waging war on Iran. Euronews reported that a vote could come as early as November 11. Trump said on November 9 that he backed Hegseth.

more.t: The UN climate conference, COP31, opened in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9 and runs through November 20; the AP reported that the U.S. was again absent.

items.h: Herzog taps Eisenkot to form Israel's next government; 46 lawmakers backed Netanyahu
items.fact: Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government on November 8 at the President's Residence in Jerusalem. Sixty-seven lawmakers recommended Eisenkot and 46 recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days, which can be extended by 14.

items.h: Rubio calls Iran's demands "outrageous"; Araghchi says "it is the White House's turn to choose"
items.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on November 8 pointed to Iran's two-day plan, under which the U.S. would carry out agreed measures on the first day and Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the second. "American voters have made their choice. Now it is the White House's turn to choose," he said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the same day that he would not say the two sides were on the verge of a breakthrough, calling Iran's demands outrageous and unrealistic.

items.h: CENTCOM launches "Iron Gate" task force to block Iran's land and Caspian trade
items.fact: U.S. Central Command said on November 7 it had launched Task Force Iron Gate to cut off advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM also said U.S. aircraft struck and stopped the cargo ship Huda in the Gulf of Oman the same day after it ignored warnings.

items.h: Trump says Ukraine will likely "end up with a little bit different shape" ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
items.fact: In a CBS "60 Minutes" interview that aired on November 8, President Donald Trump said Ukraine would likely "end up with a little bit different shape" after the war and that a deal was very close. The Kremlin had earlier said three-way talks among the U.S., Russia and Ukraine would be held in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.

items.h: Russia strikes Ukraine's grid, Black Sea ports; more than 600,000 lose power in Dnipropetrovsk
items.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 164 drones and three missiles between 6 p.m. on November 7 and 8 a.m. on November 8 local time, and that 137 drones were shot down or neutralized. DTEK said more than 600,000 residents in the Dnipropetrovsk region lost power, and Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it hit three cargo ships around Odesa, a claim that could not be verified.

items.h: Japan seeks equal treatment for Takaichi at APEC; formal summit with China unlikely, Bloomberg says
items.fact: Bloomberg reported on November 9, citing people familiar with the matter, that Japan has asked China to confirm Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will be treated like other leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19. A formal Japan-China summit is unlikely, with no more than a handshake expected, the report said.

items.h: China's factory-gate prices rise 5.7 percent in October; consumer prices up 0.7 percent
items.fact: China's National Bureau of Statistics said on November 9 that the producer price index rose 5.7 percent in October from a year earlier and the consumer price index rose 0.7 percent. Investing.com said the producer price increase was the fastest since June 2022.

more.t: Houthi rebels fired missiles at Riyadh on the morning of November 8, and an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District was damaged; Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said falling debris caused minor damage and there were no casualties.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said on November 7 that Iran has lifted its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on missile range.

A drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq's Kurdistan region at 11 p.m. local time on November 8 cut gas supplies to power plants; a Kurdistan Regional Government electricity spokesman said 2,500 to 2,800 megawatts of generating capacity was lost. No group has claimed responsibility.

Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Kirishi refinery in Russia's Leningrad region overnight on November 8–9; Governor Alexander Drozdenko said 113 drones were downed and that the Kirishi industrial zone was hit.

The Russian-installed management of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant said on November 8 that the plant lost its external power line and is running on diesel generators; Ukraine's nuclear operator Energoatom said it was the plant's 16th loss of off-site power this year.

The State Department on November 5 sanctioned two individuals, eight entities including two Chinese companies, and five vessels over the Cuban regime's foreign military support and illicit revenue networks; China's Commerce Ministry objected on November 7.

Mexico's navy said it arrested Rafael Álvarez, the alleged leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel cell "Los Rs," in Zapopan, Jalisco, on November 8, using intelligence from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration.
Military sources told Anadolu that Sudan's army and the Joint Force took Ayyal Bakhit in West Kordofan on November 7.

Citing local sources, the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said at least 30 civilians were killed in an attack in the Beni area of the Democratic Republic of the Congo overnight on November 5–6; local authorities blamed the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).

Haitian police said Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang in Cité Soleil, was neutralized by gunfire, while a Haitian rights group said he died on November 6 after a drone strike the night before.
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on November 6 that Armenia's interest in the Collective Security Treaty Organization has run its course.
In Somalia, Ibrahim Idle Suleiman was sworn in as the new head of the Supreme Court at the presidential palace on November 7; the opposition Somali Future Council called it a "coup" on November 8.
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on November 8 that Israel will not withdraw from its security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, according to AFP.

items.h: Trump says U.S. knocked out Iranian anti-aircraft device "in about 15 minutes, maybe five" in first strike since midterms
items.fact: President Donald Trump said on November 6 local time that U.S. forces had hit an anti-aircraft device Iran built, calling the strike "minor." Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island. The AP said it was the first U.S. strike since the midterms; the extent of the damage was unclear.

items.h: Qatar proposes two-day bridge deal; Iran reviewing it, Mideast officials say
items.fact: Two Middle East officials told the AP on November 6 that Qatar has proposed a plan under which, on day one, the U.S. would lift its naval blockade and return some of Iran's frozen funds and Iran would allow IAEA inspections of bombed facilities, and on day two Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. They said Iran is reviewing the plan. The White House declined to comment.

items.h: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles; Northern Bridge damaged, five injured
items.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia attacked across Ukraine with missiles, including ballistic missiles, and 172 Shahed-type drones starting at 6 p.m. local time on November 6. As of 9 a.m. on November 7, it had shot down or neutralized four missiles and 149 drones, and the attack was continuing. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern Bridge was damaged and closed to traffic in both directions, and that five people, including a 14-year-old girl, were injured.

items.h: New Zealand early count puts National-led governing coalition on track for majority
items.fact: With 10 percent of the vote counted in New Zealand's November 7 election, National had 31.2 percent, Labour 28.3 percent, ACT 11.3 percent and NZ First 9.7 percent, with the Greens at 12.7 percent, putting the governing coalition on track for a majority, AAP reported. Official results are due by November 27.

more.t: A crew member was killed in an explosion aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire on November 5; the operator suspects a missile strike, but the cause has not been confirmed, Reuters reported on November 6. The International Maritime Organization said at least 25 seafarers have been killed in the Strait of Hormuz in the conflict.

At least 30 people were killed in an attack on a market in Yemen's Taiz province on November 6, Houthi health officials told the AP. The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia; authorities aligned with the Saudi-backed government blamed the Houthis.

David Arakhamia, the ruling party's parliamentary leader, confirmed on November 6 that Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine's delegation at upcoming trilateral U.S.-Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

Elon Musk on November 5 reposted on X, without comment, another user's post saying it was a mistake for SpaceX to give Ukraine thousands of Starlink terminals and service for free, the Kyiv Independent reported on November 7.

items.h: Iran's Rezaei: no Hormuz reopening, no talks until U.S. meets seven conditions
items.fact: Iran has sent the U.S. a nuclear proposal through Qatar but will discuss it only after Washington meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions, returning frozen assets and paying war reparations, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on November 5. Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's top security official, made the same point while visiting Russia.

items.h: Nasdaq plunges 5.5 percent into correction on fears of Democratic AI curbs
items.fact: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52 percent to close at 24,315.00 on November 5, entering correction territory, while the S&P 500 lost 4.36 percent, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. The selloff was blamed on fears that Democrats, after winning control of Congress, will tighten rules on AI and data centers.

items.h: Iran claims a string of tankers hit mines near Hormuz
items.fact: Iran's military and the Revolutionary Guards said on November 5 that tankers and a tugboat caught fire after mine strikes and other incidents in waters south and east of the Strait of Hormuz. Taken together, the Iranian statements claim at least five tankers and one tug; none of the claims has been independently verified. January Brent futures settled up 3.88 percent at $98.29 a barrel that day, according to the Seoul Economic Daily.

items.h: Melania Trump hosts Russian, Ukrainian officials: "something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire"
items.fact: Melania Trump met Kirill Dmitriev, President Vladimir Putin's special envoy, and Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's parliamentary human rights commissioner, among others, at the White House on November 5 to mark a six-day truce in Oleshky, in the Kherson region, that ended November 1, and the evacuation of nearly 800 residents. President Donald Trump told reporters it would be "a big agreement" that "might involve all of Europe."

items.h: Somalia's top court rules term extension unlawful; president announces chief justice's dismissal
items.fact: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on November 5 that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension was unlawful and ordered a new agreement among political parties within 30 days and elections within 90, AFP reported. Before the ruling was published, the presidency announced it was dismissing Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed.

more.t: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned on November 5 amid the bankruptcy of digital bank Ueno; the Chamber of Deputies voted unanimously to impeach him, and Vice President Pedro Alliana will succeed him, Euronews reported.

Hoax bomb threats targeted at least 27 European passenger flights from Ireland to Bulgaria on November 5, the second such wave this week, and some made unscheduled landings, Hong Kong's The Standard reported.

The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said on November 5 that a tanker was struck by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash-Shamal, Qatar, at 11:20 p.m. GMT on November 4 (2:20 a.m. November 5 local time).

items.h: Oil plunges more than 8 percent after U.S. midterms; Brent at $94
items.fact: Brent fell 8.6 percent to $94.66 a barrel as of 1:06 p.m. ET on November 4, with WTI at $88.08, according to OilPrice.com. With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, markets are trying to gauge where the U.S.-Iran war is headed, The National reported.

items.h: Vance blames Iran war for GOP midterm losses
items.fact: Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the Iran war cost Republicans in the midterms and that "any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there," OilPrice.com reported on November 4.

items.h: Zelensky tells Witkoff, Kushner postwar guarantees must be ironclad
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he spoke for about 90 minutes on November 4 with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about Patriot interceptors and postwar security guarantees. In Brussels the same day, the U.S., Ukraine, NATO, Germany, France and the U.K. coordinated positions ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.

items.h: Indonesia's military mobilizes thousands in capital after presidential wiretap case
items.fact: Indonesia's military said it was mobilizing thousands of troops to tighten security in the capital after President Prabowo Subianto on November 4 fired his chief of staff, Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been arrested on suspicion of illegally wiretapping the president and others, Reuters reported. A presidential spokesman said the conduct could border on treason.

items.h: South Korea's Defense Ministry seeks to widen Cheonghae Unit zone south of Oman
items.fact: A revised Defense Ministry motion extending the Cheonghae Unit's deployment cleared a vice-ministerial meeting on November 5, SBS reported. It widens the unit's zone from the Gulf of Aden to south of Oman's port of Duqm and adds a P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, an explosive ordnance disposal team and unmanned mine-countermeasure systems. A ministry official said direct detection of the Strait of Hormuz or Iranian territory would be limited, Financial News reported.

more.t: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, was quoted as saying that anyone expecting a shift in U.S. policy after the midterms is badly mistaken, The National reported on November 4.

The death toll from the November 2 bombing of a school used as an aid-distribution point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 40, local officials said on November 4. Zelensky said more than 30 people may be trapped under the rubble.

Kyiv's water utility said Russia's November 3 strikes on energy infrastructure effectively cut off the city's water supply. Experts and sources called it the worst outage since the full-scale war began.

KCNA reported on November 5 that North Korea had tested a surface-to-air missile with a new guidance system and a cruise missile that drops cluster munitions on runways the previous day, NK News said.

items.h: Democrats retake Senate, projected to win House in U.S. midterms
items.fact: Democrats flipped Republican-held Senate seats in North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa and South Carolina in the November 3 midterms, winning control of the chamber, the AP reported. NBC, CNN and others projected that Democrats would also win a House majority, but the AP had not called the House as of late November 3.

items.h: Russia pounds Ukraine's grid; Kyiv says drones targeted nuclear-plant substation
items.fact: Ukrainian Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia hit power plants and substations with 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles starting early on November 3, sending three drones toward a substation critical to the stable operation of the Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plant, and that Ukraine had notified the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Grid operator Ukrenergo imposed emergency blackouts in Kyiv and several other regions.

items.h: Trump confirms strike on Iranian air-defense site, calls it a "minor attack"
items.fact: President Donald Trump said in a Fox News interview on November 3 that Iran had built an anti-aircraft facility and that "as soon as it was completed, we hit it last night," calling it a "minor attack." A U.S. official told the AP on November 2 that U.S. forces had struck Iranians who used surface-to-air missiles against them in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and elsewhere, and Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran had a legitimate right to self-defense.

items.h: Trump says he and Netanyahu agreed to end U.S. aid to Israel by year's end
items.fact: Trump said in a Fox News interview on November 3 that the U.S. gives Israel $4 billion a year but that he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "made a deal months ago that we're stopping," adding that "by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel." The current memorandum of understanding provides about $3.8 billion a year over 10 years starting in 2019; Netanyahu has previously spoken of phasing out aid over a decade, and his office did not immediately comment.

more.t: The White House said on November 3 that first lady Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives on November 5 for an event where she will speak about a localized ceasefire and civilian evacuation operation in Oleshky, in the Kherson region.

Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said, "We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal" between the U.S. and Iran, adding that Qatar was working toward an interim agreement.

items.h: Russian bombs hit aid-distribution school in Zaporizhzhia region; Ukraine says 26 killed
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 2 that a school distributing humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, and a shelter inside it were hit one after another by Russian aerial bombs, killing 26 people, and that nine more bombs fell after the first strike. Regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said 27 people were missing.

items.h: U.S. plans three-way talks with Russia, Ukraine in Abu Dhabi November 10–11, senior official says
items.fact: A senior U.S. official told Reuters on November 2 that the U.S. will hold three-way talks with Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11 on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and ending the war. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent the U.S., the official said.

items.h: Iranian negotiators leave Doha as draft deal circulates; Iran ties final deal to blockade's end
items.fact: Iranian negotiators left Doha, where they had been meeting Qatari mediators, on November 1, but not because the talks had stalled, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters on November 2. A draft deal with the U.S. is circulating and a follow-up meeting is possible, the official said. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said there will be no final deal and no reopening of the strait until the U.S. naval blockade ends and Iran's demands are met.

more.t: A local ceasefire around Oleshky in the Kherson region ended on the night of November 1 after Russia refused to extend it, and Russian forces resumed attacks on the region on November 2, Ukrainian authorities said, according to RFE/RL.

U.S. Central Command pushed back on Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's claim that Iran has not attacked civilians in neighboring countries, saying Iranian attacks have killed more than 20 civilian mariners in recent months.

items.h: U.S. warns Gulf allies of possible Iran strikes as soon as November 4, report says
items.fact: MS NOW, citing three senior Gulf Arab officials, reported that Washington warned Gulf allies that a brief but intense round of strikes on Iran could come as early as November 4, the day after the midterm elections; the White House said it does not comment on military plans. President Trump told reporters at Mar-a-Lago in Florida on October 31 that one or two of Iran's remaining nuclear-related sites still had to be dealt with, "but we can do that in 10 minutes."

items.h: Araghchi says new proposal cuts Hormuz reopening to two days as Doha talks hit day three
items.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera on October 31 that Iran had drawn up a proposal with Qatari mediators that would shorten the timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to two days. Iran's negotiators held a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on November 1, and Araghchi said no final conclusion had yet been reached.

items.h: Mojtaba Khamenei orders forces to answer any threat immediately, without geographic limits
items.fact: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, ordered the armed forces in an October 31 statement to meet any threat with an immediate, effective response unrestricted by geography, AFP reported. Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia warned on state TV on November 1 that a new war could last longer than the last one.

items.h: Tanker struck off Saudi coast; Revolutionary Guards claim two tankers hit mines in Hormuz
items.fact: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles 72 nautical miles east of Ras al-Khafji, Saudi Arabia, early on November 2 local time, and that all crew were accounted for. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed on November 1 that two tankers exploded after hitting mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz on an unauthorized route; the claim has not been verified.

loc.place: Persian Gulf, east of Ras al-Khafji (Saudi Arabia)

items.h: Russia hits Ukraine's energy facilities with 433 drones, leaving hundreds of thousands without power
items.fact: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 433 drones starting at 6 p.m. local time on October 31 and that 371 had been shot down or neutralized as of 7:30 a.m. on November 1; President Zelensky said hundreds of thousands of households were without power. Russia's Defense Ministry said it shot down 47 Ukrainian drones between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. Moscow time on November 1.

items.h: Rubio: "I don't know if negotiated peace is achievable in Ukraine"
items.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told a press conference at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on October 31, "I don't know if negotiated peace is achievable in Ukraine, that's what we're trying to find out." The three-way U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi are expected in early November, but no date has been set, the Kyiv Independent reported.

items.h: Unidentified object enters Latvian airspace near Russia, Belarus; residents told to stay indoors
items.fact: Latvia's military said on November 1 that an unidentified flying object had entered airspace around Kraslava and Ludza in the country's southeast, warning residents to stay indoors, and that the all-clear came within an hour. It said it launched an interceptor drone but had it self-destruct to avoid crossing into Russian or Belarusian airspace; the object's origin has not been determined.

items.h: France's cost-of-living protests hit third weekend: 320,000 march, 290 arrested
items.fact: Protests over the cost of living and conditions in schools drew 320,000 people across France on October 31, including 70,000 in Paris, according to authorities, marking a third straight weekend of demonstrations. The Interior Ministry reported at least 290 arrests, Al Jazeera reported; organizers claimed nearly 500,000, and police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon.

more.t: Iran designated Britain's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organizations and MI6 as a hostile group on November 1. The Foreign Ministry said the move, based on a Supreme National Security Council decision, was a reciprocal response to Britain's July designation of the Revolutionary Guards under its State Threats Act.
The FBI on October 31 blamed TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group, for the record $6.3 billion theft of crypto assets from Binance, Al Jazeera reported.
North Korea's KCNA reported on November 1 that the country tested a cluster-bomb warhead for tactical ballistic missiles on October 31; the report did not mention Kim Jong Un attending.

A European Commission spokesperson said on November 1 that the appointment of eight new Constitutional Tribunal judges lies within the constitutional power of Poland's Sejm, backing the government's position; on October 31, police formed a cordon outside the tribunal in Warsaw.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met President Zelensky in Istanbul on October 31 and said attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea are unacceptable under any circumstances, regardless of who carries them out or what justification is offered.

items.h: Oman rescues 25 from burning tanker; Revolutionary Guards claim three tankers halted
items.fact: Oman's Maritime Security Centre said on October 30 that its navy rescued 25 crew members from the RITI, a Panama-flagged tanker that caught fire after being attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the same day that three tankers using unauthorized routes were halted after incidents including mine strikes; the U.S. military has denied the mine claims, and it is unclear whether the RITI is one of the three.

items.h: Kremlin opposes truce that gives Ukraine a respite; talks date in works with U.S.
items.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on October 30 that Russia opposes a ceasefire that would give Ukraine a respite and has no plans to halt fighting before the three-way talks in Abu Dhabi, TASS reported. Presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said the same day that the talks will be held in November and that coordination on a date with Washington has begun, though no specific date has been set.

items.h: Qatari mediators return to Tehran; Trump says Iran war will be "wrapped up soon"
items.fact: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on October 30 to push for a U.S.-Iran deal in coordination with Washington, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters, while a senior Iranian official called the proposals unacceptable. President Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO the same day that the war is "going to get wrapped up soon," adding, "We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon."

items.h: Standoff in Poland over bid to suspend top court chief; president turns his plane around
items.fact: On October 30, Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the judges President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in, ordered the suspension of Constitutional Tribunal head Bogdan Święczkowski and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański. The tribunal's leadership rejected the order and called it a "coup d'état." Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote, "Restoring the rule of law is our duty." Nawrocki, en route to Senegal for a state visit, turned his plane around to return to Poland.

items.h: Canada, EU launch Alliance for the Future; Canada aims to be first EU associate member
items.fact: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen launched the Alliance for the Future at a summit in Montreal on October 30, with Canada working toward becoming the EU's first associate member, the prime minister's office said. The substance and scope of that status will be worked out over the coming months; the two sides also concluded negotiations on digital trade and competition agreements.

items.h: G20 foreign ministers' meeting opens in Atlanta with Lavrov; group photo scrapped
items.fact: A two-day G20 foreign ministers' meeting hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio opened in Atlanta on October 30, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov attending and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi sending a representative, AFP reported. A planned group photo was canceled after some European officials balked at appearing alongside Lavrov.

items.h: State Department approves $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.fact: The State Department said on October 30 it approved the possible sale to Ukraine of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles, plus parts and support, for an estimated $2.1 billion. Two people briefed on the decision said the missiles have not yet been built and are not expected to be delivered until the early 2030s, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported.

more.t: Russian and Ukrainian human rights ombudsmen carried out a humanitarian mission on October 30 in Oleshky, in Kherson region, under a local ceasefire, delivering aid and evacuating residents; the Russian side said the truce was observed.

Brazil's Foreign Ministry summoned Argentina's chargé d'affaires on October 29 to ask how defeated presidential candidate Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro left for the U.S. via Argentina, Reuters reported, citing sources; Argentina's foreign minister denied receiving a formal request.

items.h: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz; Revolutionary Guards claim three struck mines
items.fact: Britain's UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said a tanker leaving the strait was hit by an unknown projectile near Khasab, Oman, at around 8 p.m. local time on October 29. Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy claimed that over the previous 24 hours three tankers using an unauthorized southern route exploded and caught fire after hitting mines; the claim has not been independently verified.

items.h: Russian drone hits Dnipro train platform, killing 14
items.fact: A Russian drone struck a platform at Dnipro station, where a Zaporizhzhia-bound train was waiting, during the day on October 29 local time, killing 14 people and wounding 14, said Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration. Five more people were killed the same day in Chernihiv and Kremenchuk.

items.h: Iran's Tasnim says Tehran received Vance letter but has not replied
items.fact: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported on October 29 that Tehran had received a letter from U.S. Vice President JD Vance to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, but had not yet responded, and that its seven conditions still stand. President Trump said the letter was about medical supplies and that he had not ordered talks to resume.

items.h: Israel finishes count: Netanyahu bloc at 53 seats, Likud largest party with 27
items.fact: Likud won 27 seats and Yashar 21 with all votes counted, according to Central Elections Committee results released early on October 30 local time, the Times of Israel reported. By bloc, Netanyahu's has 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48 and Arab parties 19. Official results are slated to go to President Isaac Herzog on November 4.

more.t: Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on six targets in Saudi Arabia on October 29, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries, Aramco's Abqaiq facility, airports in Riyadh and Dammam, and a military headquarters in Najran. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted two ballistic missiles headed for Riyadh, and Saudi civil defense said debris injured one citizen.

South Korean National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac told lawmakers at a parliamentary audit on October 29 that Seoul is weighing options for a Strait of Hormuz deployment, including maritime patrol aircraft, in consultation with Washington, and that it will not send combat troops, Reuters reported.

North Korea's KCNA reported on October 30 that Kim Jong Un, chairman of the State Affairs Commission, attended an unmanned aviation technology exhibition on October 29, watched firings by suicide drones, 600mm multiple rocket launchers and other weapons, and called for bringing artificial intelligence into unmanned systems.

Delcy Rodríguez, who has led Venezuela since Maduro's removal, said on October 29 that elections will be held but gave no date; the same day, at a news conference in Caracas, María Corina Machado called for a presidential election in 2027.
An Italian CH-47 Chinook helicopter with the EU force in Bosnia (EUFOR) crashed during training in the Brcko area on October 29, killing four Italians and injuring 11.

items.h: Zelensky eyes Abu Dhabi talks with U.S., Russia November 6–10; Kremlin says Europe excluded
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said at a press conference with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten in The Hague on October 28 that he hopes three-way talks with the U.S. and Russia will take place in Abu Dhabi between November 6 and 10, and that Kyiv is waiting for Washington's answer. Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov told Interfax that European countries will not be included in the talks, Al Jazeera reported the same day.

items.h: Iran, mediators discuss speeding up war-ending seven-day plan; official calls Qatari draft "unacceptable ideas"
items.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X on October 28 that Tehran is "in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries" on ways to carry out the seven-day plan "in even less than a week." Reuters reported the same day that Qatari mediators handed Iran a new seven-day draft deal to end the war on October 25, and that a senior Iranian official involved in the talks called it "unacceptable ideas and not an offer."

items.h: North Korea fires about 10 short-range ballistic missiles into the East Sea from the Wonsan area
items.fact: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected about 10 short-range ballistic missiles North Korea fired from the Wonsan area into the East Sea at around 12:30 p.m. on October 29. The launch came six days after the Ministry of National Defense on October 23 proposed military talks on confirming the location of the Military Demarcation Line and restoring military communication lines, among other items; Pyongyang has not responded.

items.h: Israel count at 90 percent: Netanyahu bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48, neither with a majority
items.fact: With 89.8 percent of votes counted just after 9 p.m. local time on October 28, Central Elections Committee results put Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at 48 and Arab-led parties at a record 19, The Times of Israel reported. Roughly 430,000 to 480,000 double-envelope ballots remain, and official results will be published November 4.

items.h: Putin tells 48 African nations Russian business does not engage in "neo-colonial exploitation"
items.fact: The third Russia-Africa summit was held in Moscow on October 28 with 48 African countries represented, 22 of them by their leaders, Al Jazeera reported. President Vladimir Putin said, "Our business does not engage in the predatory, neo-colonial exploitation of natural and human resources," and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said on X the same day that his country had received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets.

more.t: Britain said on October 28 it will raise support for Ukraine by £10 billion alongside its budget, including £500 million in military aid to plug gaps in Ukraine's air defenses this winter.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited Damascus on October 28, the first trip to Syria by an Iraqi prime minister since the fall of the Assad regime, and discussed Iraqi oil exports through the Baniyas pipeline, among other issues, with President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

items.h: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority warns of legal action against Sinokor's entire fleet starting November 1
items.fact: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said on X on October 27 that vessels of South Korea's Sinokor Merchant Marine had committed the most transit violations in the Strait of Hormuz over the past three months, that it had already acted against seven of them, and that it would take legal action against all of the company's ships starting November 1. The Korea Shipowners' Association said on October 28 that the vessels in question are not owned by Sinokor but sub-chartered to an overseas oil company and carry no South Korean crew, Reuters reported.

items.h: Likud leads partial count in Israel's election as neither bloc secures a majority
items.fact: With about 40 percent of ballots counted in Israel's October 27 election, the Central Elections Committee's partial results gave Likud 21.70 percent and Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, 15.72 percent, the AP reported. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed early on October 28 that the right-wing bloc had won a decisive majority among the Zionist and Jewish public. The final tally is due by October 30, and official results will be published November 4.

items.h: Finnish and Norwegian leaders relay negotiation messages to Putin ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
items.fact: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said they spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin on October 27, in consultation with Ukraine, to convey messages on future negotiations, and that the call was linked to an upcoming meeting in Abu Dhabi. The Kyiv Independent reported that trilateral U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks are expected in Abu Dhabi sometime in November.

items.h: IAEA's Grossi tells Security Council Iran is not providing access to verify its highly enriched uranium
items.fact: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told a UN Security Council meeting on October 27 that Iran has not provided the information and access needed to verify its declared nuclear material, singling out about 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium as a particular concern. He said the agency had not detected any repair or reconstruction work at the struck facilities since June 2025.

items.h: Pezeshkian meets Putin in Moscow as Qatar urges Iran to reopen the strait
items.fact: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Russian President Vladimir Putin on October 27 on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow and said the region can resolve its problems without relying on the United States, AFP reported. Qatar's emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, also met him in Moscow that day, and Qatari foreign ministry official Ibrahim Al-Hashmi said Iran must demonstrate good faith and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

more.t: First lady Melania Trump said on X on October 27 that the Oleshky ceasefire zone had been expanded beyond Oleshky into the Kherson region to give humanitarian vehicles safe passage.
Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery on October 27; the damage has not been independently verified.

North Korea's state news agency KCNA reported on October 28 that Kim Jong Un met on October 27 with participants in the Korean People's Army's Third Conference of Company Commanders and said a company commander's foremost revolutionary task is to complete combat preparations for full wartime readiness.

items.h: Russia and Ukraine begin local ceasefire around Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
items.fact: Ukraine's parliamentary human rights commissioner, Dmytro Lubinets, said a ceasefire to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations took effect around Oleshky in Kherson Oblast at 3 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27, and Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces stopped firing in the Kherson direction at 4 a.m. Moscow time. The AP reported that the pause is due to last at least through Saturday and that a new round of U.S.-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks is expected next month.

items.h: Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv kills one, injures 10 including university dorm students
items.fact: A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late on October 26 killed one person and injured 10, including students in a university dormitory, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Ukraine's Air Force had warned that several ballistic missiles launched from the direction of Bryansk were heading for the capital; schools and medical facilities were among the sites damaged.

items.h: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani security chiefs meet Iran's leaders in Tehran, agree to keep talking
items.fact: Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met President Masoud Pezeshkian and other Iranian leaders in Tehran on October 26. Iranian state media said the four countries agreed to continue talks on strengthening cooperation; no concrete agreement was announced.

items.h: Egypt's parliament authorizes Sisi to help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
items.fact: Egypt's House of Representatives on October 26 authorized President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to take the measures needed to support Saudi Arabia, Al-Ahram reported. The authorization is conditional on a request from Riyadh, and Sisi had said earlier that any support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders and would not include attacks on Yemen.

items.h: Iran's military chief warns ships that stray from designated routes in southern waters will face damage
items.fact: Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi, chief of the general staff of Iran's armed forces, said on October 26 during a visit to the Gulf of Oman coast that any vessel that, for any reason, strays from designated routes or ignores Iranian procedures is putting itself at risk and will suffer serious damage, Press TV reported.

items.h: Romanian intelligence blames September fire near Brasov arms plant on Russian-run sabotage network
items.fact: The Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and anti-organized crime and terrorism prosecutors (DIICOT) said on October 26 that a fire on September 14 near Carfil, a subsidiary of state arms maker Romarm in Brasov, was the work of a Russian-directed sabotage network. Two of the three suspects (two Belarusians and a Ukrainian) were arrested in Germany; no casualties were reported.

items.h: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church shooting; Damascus denies prior coordination
items.fact: Jordan's armed forces said they struck hideouts of armed groups in southeastern Syria on October 26 in coordination with the Syrian government, but Damascus disputed that, saying there had been no prior coordination or notice. Syria's Civil Defense said at least seven people, including three children, were killed in Daraa and Sweida provinces.

more.t: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province and four drones headed for southern Saudi Arabia early on October 27. No casualties were reported.
At a rally in Mississippi on October 26, President Trump said the war with Iran was started by Iran, not the United States.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arrived in Moscow for the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit and is expected to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin.

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said on October 27 that it assesses the North Korean self-propelled guns spotted along the coast of Kaepung County in Hwanghae Province to be older models and is closely watching the intent behind their exposure.

items.h: Kim Jong Un makes day trip to China's Dandong, greeted by Wang Huning
items.fact: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 for a one-day visit to Dandong in China's Liaoning province, laying a wreath at the memorial to China's Korean War intervention and touring a car factory, according to Xinhua (October 24) and KCNA (October 25). Wang Huning, chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, received him and saw him off; no meeting with Xi Jinping was reported.

items.h: Kremlin aide Ushakov says U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks can resume after November 4
items.fact: Yuri Ushakov, the Kremlin's foreign policy aide, told Russian TV channel Vesti on October 25 that the next deadline is November 4, a Russian national holiday, and that Moscow is ready to resume talks after that. He said the first meeting would be preliminary, RBC reported.

items.h: Trump on new Iran strikes: "maybe tomorrow" — then "There will not be a strike today"
items.fact: Asked on October 24 (local time) whether the U.S. would strike Iran again, President Trump told reporters, "We're thinking about doing it, and maybe tomorrow." On October 25, at the White House before leaving for a rally in Michigan, he said, "There will not be a strike today." He did not say whether he had made a decision.

items.h: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco site in Yanbu; Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles
items.fact: Yemen's Houthis claimed on October 24 that they struck an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh refinery and other targets in Saudi Arabia; no damage has been confirmed. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif on October 24 and 10 aimed at southern Saudi Arabia on October 25, among others.

items.h: Iran says it is trading messages with the U.S. through intermediaries
items.fact: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei told a German broadcaster that Iran remains open to diplomacy and is passing messages to the U.S. through intermediaries, but that Iran cannot accept demands for "complete surrender," Iranian state media reported. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on October 25 that Iran's policies stay the same whether or not there is war.

items.h: North Korea claims to UN Security Council that South staged DMZ mine blast
items.fact: North Korea sent a letter on October 25 to the president of the UN Security Council calling the September 21 mine explosion in the DMZ a South Korean fabrication and warning that it would exercise its right of self-defense if its territory or personnel were violated, KCNA reported on October 26. North Korean media have not reported the South Korean Defense Ministry's October 23 proposal for military talks.

items.h: Student movement wins Serbia's election as Vučić concedes defeat
items.fact: Former President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary election, citing a sample count. He said the Student List would win 135 to 140 of the 250 seats and his own camp about 105.

items.h: Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil's presidential runoff
items.fact: Brazil's Superior Electoral Court declared President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva the winner of the October 25 runoff with 51.76 percent of the vote against 48.24 percent for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a margin of more than 4 million votes.

items.h: Machado returns to Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile
items.fact: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home on October 25 after more than 10 months in exile and greeted supporters at a church in Lara state. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said her return was the result of U.S.-backed reconciliation talks.

more.t: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 153 drones overnight on October 24–25 and that 119 were shot down or neutralized; Ukrainian authorities said a Russian attack on the Dnipro area on the night of October 24 killed four people.

Elon Musk claimed Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms of service by using it for offensive drone strikes; Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to President Zelensky, countered that commercial Starlink cannot be used for long- or medium-range strikes.
Iran's Tasnim news agency claimed on October 25 that army air defenses shot down a U.S. drone over Bandar Abbas; the claim has not been independently verified.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned on October 25 that Iran or its proxies could attack to disrupt Israel's October 27 general election.

Yonhap reported that what appears to be a North Korean 122mm self-propelled gun, its barrel pointed south, was spotted on the morning of October 25 in a coastal border area of Kaepung County, Hwanghae Province, as seen from the Aegibong observatory in Gimpo.

items.h: Cargo ship sinks after drone strike just outside Romanian waters; Romania's president blames Russia
items.fact: The Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv sank on October 23 after a drone strike about 13 nautical miles off the Romanian port of Constanta, just beyond Romania's territorial waters. One Ukrainian sailor was killed and three crew members are missing. Romanian President Nicusor Dan called the attack part of Russia's escalation of its war in Ukraine; Russia had not publicly responded.

items.h: Trump on Iran: "We may do another little Epic Fury"
items.fact: At a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on October 23, President Trump said of the Iran war, "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree." Operation Epic Fury is the U.S. military's name for its campaign against Iran.

items.h: Asked about a weekend strike on Iran, U.S. ambassador Barrack says "absolutely"; Trump says he knows nothing about it
items.fact: Asked in an interview released October 23 whether a strike could come this weekend, Tom Barrack, the U.S. ambassador to Turkey, answered, "Absolutely." Trump said the same day that he didn't know anything about it. He had said earlier that a strike would not come before the November 3 midterm elections.

items.h: Zelensky says technical-level U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks are planned in Abu Dhabi for the first half of November
items.fact: In a video address to the Hudson Institute on October 23, President Zelensky said negotiating teams from the U.S., Russia and Ukraine plan to meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November. If the technical-level talks are productive, he said, they should move to a meeting of leaders; an October meeting fell through because Russia cited other reasons.

items.h: Ukraine and Russia agree to a local ceasefire around Oleshky, mediated by Melania Trump
items.fact: The White House and Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said on October 23 that first lady Melania Trump had mediated a local ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast. The truce is meant to allow civilian evacuations and aid deliveries. Russia's General Staff said it would begin at 4 a.m. local time on October 27; the White House gave the start date as October 29.

items.h: State Department cuts embassy staff in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE over Houthi threat
items.fact: The State Department said on October 23 that it is reducing staff at its embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, which will remain open, citing concerns about Houthi rocket, missile and drone attacks, CBS reported. Nonessential staff at the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia were ordered to leave earlier in the week.

items.h: Brent settles at $116.72, its highest close since April 29
items.fact: Brent crude futures settled at $116.72 a barrel on October 23, up 3.14 percent, and U.S. West Texas Intermediate closed at $103.27, up 3.8 percent, according to Reuters. Reuters said Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoked fears of supply disruptions.

items.h: Waltz on the prospect of another year of war in Iran: "One would hope" Tehran comes to the table first
items.fact: Asked by the Financial Times whether the Iran war could last another year, Mike Waltz, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, declined to speculate but said, "One would hope that they'll come to the table in a meaningful way before that." He added that the U.S. Navy can maintain the naval blockade of Iran for the foreseeable future.

items.h: Ukraine and Russia swap 270 prisoners each, the first exchange in two months
items.fact: President Zelensky said on October 23 that 270 Ukrainian prisoners of war had come home and 270 Russian POWs had been returned to Russia. It was the first swap since August; most of the returning Ukrainians were captured during the 2022 siege of Mariupol.

items.h: Seoul proposes military talks with North Korea to verify the MDL and restore hotlines
items.fact: In a statement on the afternoon of October 23, Kim Hong-cheol, South Korea's deputy minister for national defense policy, formally proposed military talks with the North to jointly verify where the land Military Demarcation Line lies, restore military communication lines and discuss ways to prevent accidental clashes along the border. He said three-way talks including the UN Command were also possible.

more.t: CBS News reported on October 23 that Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a memo that lethal Iranian plots against Americans had "reached advanced stages."

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on October 23 that Iran-Russia talks attended by both presidents would take place next week, and Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that President Masoud Pezeshkian will attend a summit of gas-exporting countries in Moscow on October 27.

Foreign ministers from Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt met in Istanbul on October 23 to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen and the Russia-Ukraine war, AFP reported.
South Korea's military told lawmakers on October 23 that North Korea is estimated to have laid about 960,000 land mines in the Demilitarized Zone since 2024.
Moldovan President Maia Sandu said on October 23 that Moldova had declared a Russian embassy staffer persona non grata after a Russian Geran drone came down near homes in central Moldova.

items.h: Trump on Iran: "We may do it a little bit further"
items.fact: Speaking to reporters at the White House on October 22 before leaving for a rally in Iowa, President Trump said, "We've knocked the hell out of them, and we may do it a little bit further." He added, "We can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

items.h: Trump claims Iran is "making up fake hits, mines" to push up oil prices
items.fact: In a Truth Social post on October 22, Trump claimed Iran "is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election" and is "making up fake hits, mines, and everything else." Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed the same day that four tankers had been hit and three had struck mines; the claims could not be independently verified.

items.h: IRGC threatens U.S. bases over Hormuz tanker transits
items.fact: The IRGC warned on October 22, in a statement on its Sepah News site, that U.S. help for tankers transiting the strait could widen the war: "If this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region." A U.S. Central Command spokesperson, speaking to Al Jazeera on condition of anonymity, called the mine claims incorrect and said 95 percent of vessels are getting through.

items.h: Brent settles at $113, its highest close since early May
items.fact: Brent crude rose 4.0 percent on October 22 to settle at $113.17 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude gained 2.4 percent to $99.47. It was Brent's highest settlement since May 4.

items.h: Saudi airport attack death toll rises to two; coalition intercepts missile aimed at Najran
items.fact: Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said on October 22 that the death toll from the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam had risen to two. The Saudi-led coalition said the same day it had intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Najran, and AFP, citing sources, reported that Aramco told essential staff at its Dhahran headquarters to evacuate.

items.h: Reuters: U.S. and South Korean officials see little chance of a Trump-Kim meeting this year
items.fact: Citing five people familiar with the matter, Reuters reported that U.S. and South Korean officials see little chance of a meeting this year between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The sources said Washington has received no response from Pyongyang on holding one.

items.h: Zelensky: Kyiv strike right after talks shows "no real change" in Russia's attitude
items.fact: Zelensky said on social media on October 22 that Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves from the evening of October 21 into the early hours of October 22 (local time), and also used three ballistic missiles fitted with cluster warheads. He said 12 regions came under attack and 34 people were wounded, five of them children.

items.h: Kremlin says Abu Dhabi is the venue under discussion for three-way talks
items.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on October 22 that "at this point, we are talking about Abu Dhabi" as the venue for talks among Russia, the U.S. and Ukraine. Asked whether Russia's negotiators were preparing documents or proposals, he declined to say, telling reporters not to get ahead of themselves.

more.t: CENTCOM said on October 22 that 100 days had passed since it reinstated its naval blockade of Iran, with no seaborne exports or imports other than humanitarian aid cleared by U.S. forces, and that it had blocked more than $25 billion in Iranian crude exports.
Yemen's Defense Ministry said on October 22 that it would treat Houthi rallies and mobilization events as legitimate military targets and warned residents of Houthi-held areas not to take part.

Asked on October 22 about Philippine plans to work with Taiwan on undersea cables and gray-zone challenges, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said, "There is no gray zone on the Taiwan question," and urged Manila to abide by the one-China principle.

French President Emmanuel Macron described last weekend's riots as seditious acts by the "ultra-left," and authorities banned protests on October 22 around the Élysée Palace, parliament and major stations in Paris and in Lyon, Lille and Grenoble. Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said more than 2,700 people had been detained.
A government representative in Chad's Wadi Fira province told AFP that a drone of unknown origin struck Bamina, a town on the Sudanese border, this week, killing four people and wounding 14.

items.h: Kremlin says it is ready to resume three-way talks around November 10 after Witkoff meeting
items.fact: After Putin met U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21, presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia is ready in principle to resume three-way talks with the U.S. and Ukraine around November 10. Russia freed jailed American Stephen Hubbard, 74, as the meeting began.

items.h: Zelensky hopes for U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks by early November
items.fact: On his way back to Kyiv from Norway, Zelensky told reporters he believes the three-way talks should take place no later than early November (Al Jazeera, October 21). Ushakov told Russian state TV channel Vesti the talks could be held in Abu Dhabi.

items.h: Netanyahu says toppling Iran's regime is the only way to end its threat
items.fact: Speaking at an Israeli military officers' graduation ceremony on October 21, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the only way to remove Iran's threat for good is to overthrow the regime. He said he had issued directives to the military, the Mossad and other security services but did not say what they were.

items.h: State Department orders non-emergency staff and families out of Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks
items.fact: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X on October 21 that the department had ordered non-emergency employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi airports and infrastructure. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said an attack late on October 21 on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight.

items.h: IRGC spokesman warns Iran will respond and go on the offensive if attacked
items.fact: In an October 21 interview with the Student News Network, IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said the Guards' doctrine, which had been largely defensive, now includes offensive action, and that any country that attacks Iran will face both a response and an offensive, IranWire reported.

items.h: Kim Yo Jong says loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be on standby within days
items.fact: In an October 22 statement carried by KCNA, Kim Yo Jong, director of the Workers' Party's General Affairs Department, said North Korea's new means of response will go on mission standby along the entire border and its loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be on standby within days. In an October 21 statement, she said the loudspeakers would be operating along the entire border sometime in October.

items.h: Russian ballistic missiles and drones hit Kyiv overnight October 21–22, injuring 15
items.fact: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks overnight on October 21–22 (local time) injured 15 people, including two 15-year-olds. Metro infrastructure on the Pivdennyi Bridge and an ambulance station in the Pecherskyi district were damaged.

items.h: Moscow mayor reports downing drones overnight October 21–22; TASS tallies 630
items.fact: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported downing wave after wave of Ukrainian drones headed for Moscow between 8:30 p.m. on October 21 and 4 a.m. on October 22 (Moscow time); TASS, tallying his announcements, put the total at 630. He said 163 were downed as they approached the city, and two people were injured near Voronovo.

items.h: U.S. Embassy in Canada accuses Canadian politicians of trying to sway the midterms
items.fact: In a fact sheet released October 21, the U.S. Embassy in Canada claimed that Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, Ontario Premier Doug Ford and others are trying to influence the November 3 U.S. midterm elections through their responses to President Donald Trump's tariffs. Joly had denied any interference on October 14, saying her work in the U.S. was aimed at attracting investment.

more.t: In a joint statement in Doha on October 21, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and French President Emmanuel Macron called for restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz without constraints or fees and for implementing the Gaza ceasefire.
Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said October 21 that debris from a drone intercepted as it headed for the Shaybah oil field in the east killed two people and injured two.
Mexican authorities on October 21 charged former Chihuahua state Attorney General César Jáuregui with treason for allowing U.S. agents to take part in an anti-drug operation.

items.h: Witkoff to take Oslo proposals to Russian leaders in St. Petersburg on October 21
items.fact: After talks in Oslo on October 20 with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre told reporters that Witkoff would take the Oslo proposals to the Russian side in St. Petersburg on October 21 and try to pave the way for a U.S.-Ukraine-Russia leaders' meeting.

items.h: Zelensky says U.S. intelligence is flowing again: "We are thankful that intelligence works now"
items.fact: At a joint press conference in Oslo on October 20, Zelensky said U.S. early warning of Russian ballistic missile launches is flowing again. He also said the negotiating document contains several kinds of security guarantees, which Witkoff will pass on to Russia.

items.h: Trump says Zelensky "has to want to settle this war" or it will be "a very bad thing"
items.fact: Speaking at the White House on October 20, President Trump said Russia has an "unlimited" supply of manpower and that Zelensky "has to want to settle this war, and if he doesn't, I think it's going to be a very bad thing." On a possible Putin-Zelensky meeting, he cited "tremendous" hatred between the two and said, "I don't care how it's done."

items.h: Russian drones kill one, injure 18 in Kyiv on October 20
items.fact: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian attacks on the capital on October 20 killed one person and injured 18. The city health department had counted one dead and 12 injured since midnight as of 5:50 p.m. local time.

items.h: Araghchi says Hormuz reopens only if the U.S. accepts Iran's terms; Rezaei rules out shipping out "a single gram" of enriched uranium
items.fact: In an interview with Iraq's Al-Ikhbariya on October 20, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that under Iran's seven-day plan the Strait of Hormuz was to have fully reopened on the sixth day, and that Washington must honor its commitments under the Islamabad memorandum. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, ruled out shipping any enriched uranium out of Iran in a post on X the same day.

items.h: Chinese coast guard ship goes dark, enters restricted waters off Pratas and faces off with Taiwan
items.fact: Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration said on October 20 that a China Coast Guard ship, its automatic identification system (AIS) switched off, entered restricted waters northeast of the Pratas Islands early that day and faced off with the Taiwanese patrol vessel Taichung. The Chinese ship broadcast that "the so-called Republic of China does not exist."

items.h: Death toll from drone strike on market in disputed Abyei rises to at least 153
items.fact: Yohanna Akol Ngor, caretaker information minister for the Abyei administration, said a drone strike around 11 a.m. local time on October 19 on the Amiet market and a nearby fuel depot killed at least 153 people, and blamed Sudan's military. A senior Sudanese officer, speaking anonymously, said the army targeted fuel tankers bound for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

loc.place: Abyei (disputed by Sudan and South Sudan)

items.h: Nigeria confirms Ebola case in woman from Uganda, traces 44 contacts
items.fact: Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare said a woman who traveled from Uganda tested positive for Ebola in Abuja, and Health Minister Muhammad Pate said 44 contacts are being traced, Al Jazeera reported on October 20. Congo has recorded more than 9,000 cases since May in an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain, which has no licensed vaccine.

more.t: South Korea's Foreign Ministry said at its regular briefing on October 20 that it will withdraw some staff from its embassy in Ukraine (about half, according to a ministry official), leaving a chargé d'affaires and consular staff, citing a high threat of air strikes and Kyiv's failure to take "forward-looking measures" over its public disclosure of the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war.

A spokesperson for the PLA Southern Theater Command Navy said on October 20 that the U.S. littoral combat ship USS Charleston entered waters near Sabina Shoal in the South China Sea without permission and demanded that the U.S. side "immediately cease such activities."

The websites of Rodong Sinmun and the Korean Central News Agency have been unreachable since the evening of October 20 and remained down as of the morning of October 21, according to South Korea's Unification Ministry and others.
Kharkiv Governor Oleh Syniehubov said a Russian drone attack on the village of Korotych overnight on October 20–21 killed two residents in their 80s.

items.h: Kim Yo Jong says North's military weighs restarting loudspeakers, adding tactical strike assets
