items.fact: Kim Yo Jong, director of the Workers' Party's General Affairs Department, said in an October 19 statement carried by state media that the situation on the southern border was very unstable, and claimed South Korean troops issued 2,870 warning broadcasts and fired warning shots 201 times between August 1 and October 17. South Korea's Defense Ministry on October 20 expressed grave concern and vowed a decisive response if Pyongyang uses this as a pretext for further provocations.

items.h: Hegseth made unannounced Israel trip to meet Netanyahu, Axios reports
items.fact: Axios reported October 19, citing two sources, that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced trip to Israel and met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu; the Pentagon declined to comment. The same day, Netanyahu posted video of a call with President Trump on X in which he said, "Donald, we have a job to finish," invoking Iran.

items.h: Houthi missile strike on Yemeni government base in Shabwa kills 53
items.fact: A spokesperson for Yemeni government forces said the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles on October 19 at the al-Alam base in Shabwa, where new recruits were training; local authorities in Shabwa said 53 people were killed and 200 wounded. The Houthis claimed the attack, saying they targeted a Saudi-backed base.

items.h: Russian drone strike on Kharkiv-region park in Nova Vodolaha kills six, including three children
items.fact: Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, said October 19 that a Russian drone struck a park in central Nova Vodolaha, killing six people, three of them children. President Zelensky called for sanctions on Russia to stay in place as long as the killings continue.

items.h: Zelensky offers 30-day pause on refinery strikes in exchange for Patriot help
items.fact: On an October 19 video call with a bipartisan U.S. congressional delegation, Zelensky said Kyiv had offered to stop striking Russian oil refineries for 30 days if the U.S. provided Patriot air-defense support for that period. He also said Russia had rejected a mutual halt to energy strikes and that partners gave no advance warning of recent ballistic missile attacks.

items.h: Witkoff to hold Oslo talks this week before meeting Putin, Reuters reports
items.fact: Reuters reported October 19, citing people familiar with the plans, that envoy Steve Witkoff is expected to meet Zelensky and representatives of Britain, France, Germany, Poland, the EU and NATO in Norway this week before traveling to Russia to see Putin, though the schedule could change.

items.h: In Tehran, Lavrov says Russian specialists will return to Bushehr in stages
items.fact: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran on October 19 and said Russian specialists who left the Bushehr nuclear plant during the war would gradually return. Araghchi said the insecurity around the Strait of Hormuz is a direct result of U.S. and Israeli military attacks.

items.h: Alberta voters reject starting a separation process as 76 percent vote to stay in Canada
items.fact: In Alberta's October 19 referendum, with more than 1 million votes counted, about 76 percent chose to remain in Canada and about 23 percent backed starting a process toward a separation vote; CBC projected on October 20 that Alberta would stay.

items.h: France orders partial curfews in Paris, Lyon, Nice and Lille after violent protests
items.fact: At Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's request, prefects on October 19 imposed partial overnight curfews around Place de la République and Les Halles in Paris (11 p.m. October 19 to 6 a.m. October 20) and in Lyon, Nice, Lille and elsewhere, some covering only minors. Lecornu said the government could declare a state of emergency if needed.

more.t: Egypt's state news agency MENA said October 19 that parliament had postponed until October 26 its vote authorizing the military to defend Saudi Arabia.
Maha Al Saud, CEO of the FII Institute, said October 19 that the Future Investment Initiative conference in Riyadh, set for October 26–29, will move to 2027.
Russia's Defense Ministry said it downed 136 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over 14 regions between 8 p.m. October 19 and 8 a.m. October 20, Moscow time.

Randall Schriver, chair of the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, told a forum in Taipei on October 20 that Chinese coast guard patrols east of Taiwan would be "highly destabilizing if they continue to operationalize this law enforcement role."

items.h: Russian missiles and drones hit Kyiv and other regions; one killed, eight injured in the capital
items.fact: Russia launched 269 drones along with ballistic and cruise missiles overnight on October 18–19, Ukraine's air force said, adding that 243 drones and four missiles were shot down or neutralized and that hits were recorded at 25 locations. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it struck a data center in Kyiv and a locomotive depot it said was used to store missiles, as well as a cargo ship at sea 130 kilometers southwest of Odesa.

items.h: WSJ: Putin proposed a three-way Ukraine summit with Trump and Xi
items.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported on October 18 (U.S. time) that Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed discussing an end to the war in Ukraine with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19, without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there was no clear understanding yet about the meeting or its agenda, and a senior U.S. official said Trump had not agreed but might be open to it.

items.h: Zelensky claims U.S. has cleared only some of the Patriot missiles already paid for
items.fact: In a Bloomberg interview published October 18, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Washington had approved delivery of only some of the Patriot missiles bought through PURL, the program that uses NATO allies' money to buy U.S. weapons, and that this was not a technical issue. He also claimed that steps had been taken to convince Ukraine to capitulate.

items.h: Rubio says Ukraine currently has no access to Starshield, denies ordering a speed cap
items.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on October 17 that Ukraine does not currently have access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink, and that its request is under discussion. He called reports that the White House ordered Starlink speeds slowed "categorically false," though Ukrainian defense officials had earlier said Starshield was working again.

items.h: North Korea-China trade hits $299 million in September, up 18.6 percent year to date
items.fact: North Korea-China trade came to about $299 million in September, up from $238 million in August and the year's second-highest monthly total after April, according to China's General Administration of Customs data released October 18 and reported by NK News, a North Korea-focused outlet. By the Sankei Shimbun's count, trade from January through September totaled about $2.27 billion, up 18.6 percent from a year earlier.

items.h: Massive drone attack sets St. Petersburg oil terminal ablaze, killing one
items.fact: St. Petersburg Gov. Alexander Beglov said on October 18 that a "massive" drone attack killed one person, injured five and set fire to an oil terminal and a fuel depot, among other sites. Russia's Defense Ministry said it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones between 8 p.m. on October 17 and 8 a.m. on October 18.

items.h: Rubio says Trump wants up to 60 days to weigh impact of waived Russia sanctions, tariffs
items.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on October 17 that President Trump plans to spend up to 60 days analyzing the economic effects of the Russia sanctions and tariffs he waived on October 16. The October 16 executive order itself sets no end date for the waiver.

items.h: Zelensky says U.S. proposed three-way talks, but Moscow and Washington have yet to confirm
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told reporters on October 17 that the United States had proposed a trilateral meeting but that neither Russia nor the U.S. had yet confirmed it. He said possible venues include a Middle Eastern country such as the UAE or Saudi Arabia, the U.S. during the G20 summit, or a European country.

items.h: IRGC claims another 'noncompliant' tanker hit a mine south of Hormuz
items.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy claimed early on October 19, Tehran time, that a tanker leaving the strait by an unauthorized southern route with its navigation systems switched off struck a mine, causing an explosion and fire in its engine room. It did not name the ship, and there was no independent confirmation.

items.h: Projectile hits residential area in Saudi Arabia's Najran, injuring six
items.fact: Saudi Civil Defense said on October 18 that a projectile fell on a residential area of Najran, injuring six civilians and damaging three homes and three vehicles; Saudi media attributed it to the Houthis. The same day, a Saudi military helicopter crashed in Najran, killing two officers.

items.h: Taiwan's coast guard drives off 16 Chinese ships, accuses Beijing of hybrid warfare
items.fact: Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration said on October 18 it drove away 16 Chinese vessels, including coast guard ships, research vessels and fishing boats, off the main island's eastern, southern and southwestern coasts and around the Pratas Islands, adding that some had entered restricted waters. It condemned China for waging hybrid warfare at several locations at once to change the status quo unilaterally.

items.h: Trump fully endorses Netanyahu nine days before Israel's election
items.fact: In an October 18 Truth Social post, President Trump gave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu his "Complete and Total Endorsement," saying the U.S. would soon finish the job unless Iran changes course and that with any other leader it would have to do so itself, which he is not inclined to do. Israel votes on October 27.

items.h: Pakistani troops and Afghan Taliban clash on the border in Kurram
items.fact: Pakistani security officials claimed that troops fought Afghan Taliban forces for hours at several points along the border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province's Kurram district on October 17 and that artillery-backed units destroyed Taliban posts. The Taliban government had no immediate comment, and there was no confirmed casualty count.

items.h: French protests spiral into riots and looting, with at least 1,800 arrested
items.fact: Protests by about 550,000 people across France on October 17, by the authorities' count, over rising living costs and worsening school conditions descended into arson and looting. At least 1,800 people were arrested, according to a CBS News tally; Al Jazeera, citing the Interior Ministry, put the number at about 2,400. In a televised address on October 18, President Emmanuel Macron said looters would have to pay for the damage.

more.t: Zelensky said in an NBC interview on October 18 that the U.S. has resumed sharing intelligence on Russian missile launches, and he spoke by phone the same day with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in Baghdad on October 18 that Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table.
Iranian media reported that Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov will visit Tehran on October 19.
Egypt's parliament postponed until October 19 a vote on authorizing military support for Saudi Arabia.

Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda said on October 18 that what appeared to be a drone entered Lithuanian airspace and exploded; a Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson apologized, saying Russian electronic warfare may have pushed a Ukrainian drone off course.

items.h: Trump waives most tariffs and sanctions under the Graham Russia sanctions law two days before they take effect
items.fact: President Trump signed an executive order on October 16 waiving most of the tariffs and sanctions in the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which were set to take effect October 18, and certified to Congress that the move serves the national interest. The waiver also covers 100 percent additional tariffs on the five largest importers of Russian oil and gas, and it sets no expiration date.

items.h: Russia launches massive attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, hitting more than 15 power facilities
items.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia fired 332 drones plus ballistic and cruise missiles between 6 p.m. on October 16 and the morning of October 17, and that 293 were shot down or neutralized; President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 15 power generation and transmission facilities were attacked. Russia's Defense Ministry said it struck targets including a steel plant in Zaporizhzhia and a transformer factory run by Ukraine's Defense Ministry.

items.h: Gerasimov claims capture of Dobropillia; Ukraine's General Staff denies it
items.fact: Valery Gerasimov, chief of Russia's General Staff, reported to President Vladimir Putin on October 16 that Russian forces had captured Dobropillia in the Donetsk region. Andrii Kovalov, a spokesman for Ukraine's General Staff, said on October 17 that the claim was false and that the town remains under the control of Ukrainian forces.

items.h: IRGC claims a 'violating' supertanker struck a mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz
items.fact: The navy of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed on October 17 that a "violating" supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude hit a mine and exploded while crossing the Strait of Hormuz on an "unauthorized" route with its location and radar systems switched off. The IRGC did not name the ship or give its exact location.

items.h: UKMTO says two tankers were hit off Jubail, Saudi Arabia
items.fact: The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said on October 17 that two tankers were hit on October 16 northeast of Jubail, Saudi Arabia: one about 68 nautical miles out by an unknown projectile, the other about 78 nautical miles out by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat. All crew members were safe, and it was not clear who carried out the attacks.

items.h: Egypt's Sisi asks parliament for emergency session to authorize defending Saudi Arabia
items.fact: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, speaking at a military academy graduation on October 17, asked parliament to hold an emergency session to authorize action to protect Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it. He said he had no intention of attacking anyone and would only defend Saudi Arabia.

items.h: North Korea says it tested a new ultra-high-speed precision-guided torpedo using AI
items.fact: North Korea's Korean Central News Agency reported on October 17 that a new ultra-high-speed precision-guided torpedo, with AI technology applied to its target detection and guidance functions, was successfully test-fired underwater on October 15.

more.t: Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, said on October 16 that "the Strait of Hormuz is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran."
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in Yerevan, Armenia, on October 16 that Iran does not seek nuclear weapons and is ready for dialogue.

Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the tanker ST 3, with 15 Indian seafarers aboard, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 16 and that all crew members were safe.

European Council President António Costa said after the October 16 summit that leaders had identified the means to cover Ukraine's financing needs for this year and had asked the European Commission for a proposal on its additional needs for 2027.
Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, introduced bipartisan legislation on October 16 to block the Russian diesel purchase deal proposed by President Trump.

items.h: Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian refineries; fire breaks out at Ryazan plant
items.fact: President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times, in an interview published October 15, that he had lifted the restriction on striking Russian oil refineries. Russia's Defense Ministry said the same day that it shot down four cruise missiles and 69 drones aimed at the Ryazan refinery, and Ryazan Governor Pavel Malkov said the refinery caught fire.

items.h: Zelensky says Russia launched more than 850 drones; three killed in Kirovohrad region
items.fact: Zelensky said Russia fired more than 850 attack drones between midnight October 14 and 9 a.m. October 15, hitting dozens of cities and villages. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said a drone attack lasting more than 10 hours killed three people and injured six in the Kirovohrad region.

items.h: Iran's military claims Hormuz fully closed; reports fire on 'violating' tanker
items.fact: The Iranian army's navy said on October 15 that a "violating" oil tanker caught fire while trying to cross a "forbidden region" east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking system switched off, without naming the ship or the cause of the fire. Habibollah Sayyari, the army's deputy chief of staff for coordination, claimed the same day that the strait was completely closed.

items.h: Houthis fire missiles at presidential palace in Aden; five killed
items.fact: Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said on October 15 that the Houthis fired five missiles at the al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden, and the health minister said five people were killed and 16 wounded. The Houthis claimed they had targeted a Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden.

items.h: Lavrov says there will be no ceasefire that lets Ukraine rearm
items.fact: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told a news conference in Baku on October 15 that the objectives of the special military operation and Russia's position on the Ukraine conflict had not changed. Russian media reported that he said there would be no ceasefire allowing Ukraine to rearm.

items.h: Seoul defense spokesperson, speaking personally, says shifting requirements could stall OPCON transfer
items.fact: A spokesperson for South Korea's Ministry of National Defense told a regular briefing on October 15 that wartime operational control (OPCON) could not be transferred if the requirements kept changing, adding that this was a personal view. Gen. Xavier Brunson, commander of U.S. Forces Korea, said in Washington on October 14 that the conditions and the plan had changed and new standards had to be met.

more.t: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 149 drones between 6 p.m. on October 15 and the morning of October 16, that 114 were shot down or neutralized, and that 24 locations were hit.
Putin claimed at a congress of the business group Delovaya Rossiya on October 15 that Ukraine had struck Wildberries and Ozon warehouses first and that Russia had begun to respond.

Ukrainian defense officials said Starshield, the military version of Starlink, was working again on moving terminals after more than a day of restrictions, though Ukraine's top diplomat in Washington said speeds had not fully recovered.
An EU summit in Brussels ended its first day on October 15 without agreement on the next long-term budget; on October 16, the second day, leaders will discuss support for Ukraine with Zelensky.

Chinese Commerce Ministry spokesperson He Yadong said on October 15 that China would keep expediting the review and approval of rare earth export licenses for Europe and hoped the EU would respond by helping resolve dual-use export license issues for Chinese companies.

items.h: Ukraine's air force counts 39 Russian missiles and 128 drones; 600,000 lose power
items.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 39 missiles and 128 drones between 6 p.m. on October 13 and the morning of October 14, Kyiv time, and that four missiles and 115 drones were shot down or neutralized. President Volodymyr Zelensky said at least 600,000 people lost power.

items.h: Russia's Defense Ministry claims strikes on six power plants around Kyiv and Kharkiv
items.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said on October 14 that its forces had struck the No. 4, 5 and 6 combined heat and power plants and the Trypillia thermal power plant near Kyiv, two plants near Kharkiv, and a data center in Kyiv with ground-launched precision weapons and long-range drones. It claimed the sites supported Ukraine's armed forces and defense industry.

items.h: North Korea test-fires two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in the East Sea
items.fact: The Korean Central News Agency reported on October 15 that North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in the East Sea on October 14. It said the test was meant to verify the navy's mission capabilities and the reliability of its war deterrent, and claimed it had no negative impact on the security of neighboring countries.

items.h: Singapore-flagged container ship sinks in Strait of Hormuz after projectile strike
items.fact: Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) said on October 14 that the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride had sunk in the Strait of Hormuz and that all 21 crew members were evacuated. The ship caught fire after being hit by a projectile on October 13. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a container ship sank after hitting a mine but did not name the vessel.

items.h: Houthis claim they targeted Riyadh's King Khalid airport; coalition intercepts ballistic missile
items.fact: Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, said on October 14 that the coalition had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile the Houthis fired toward Riyadh. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the group had targeted King Khalid International Airport.

items.h: U.S. consumer prices rise 3.7 percent in September as gasoline jumps 34.2 percent
items.fact: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said on October 14 that consumer prices in September were 3.7 percent higher than a year earlier. Energy prices rose 20.4 percent and gasoline 34.2 percent, while core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 2.6 percent.

more.t: Russia's Defense Ministry said it shot down 902 Ukrainian drones over several Russian regions, Crimea and the Sea of Azov overnight from October 13 into the morning of October 14.
Zelensky met British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in London on October 14, and Burnham said Britain would speed up deliveries of British-made air defenses.

Serhii Beskrestnov, a technology adviser to Zelensky, said SpaceX had imposed a speed limit on Starlink terminals in motion so that military terminals stop working above 160 kilometers per hour, disrupting operations.

Reuters, citing Iranian officials, reported that Iran shifted tactics in its attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz about 10 days ago to keep oil prices high and influence the U.S. midterm elections.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Army Radio on October 14 that a preemptive strike on Iran before the October 27 election would not be good for Israel.

items.h: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv power plant and apartment building, killing two
items.fact: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles at about 10:40 p.m. local time on October 13, hitting an apartment building in the Desnianskyi district and the grounds of the city's Combined Heat and Power Plant No. 4. The Kyiv Post reported early on October 14 that two people had been killed and 21 injured.

items.h: Russia says it intercepted 604 Ukrainian drones, 417 of them headed for Moscow
items.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 604 Ukrainian drones over 15 regions and the Sea of Azov between 8 p.m. on October 12 and 8 a.m. on October 13, Moscow time. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 417 of them were flying toward the Moscow area.

items.h: Trump on whether Russia broke the energy ceasefire: "I'll let you know about that later"
items.fact: Asked at the White House on October 13 whether Russia had violated the energy ceasefire, President Trump said he would let reporters know later, adding that Ukraine had hit many sites the day before. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, he said, should focus on making a deal rather than talking about that.

items.h: UKMTO says tanker and container ship hit by unidentified projectiles in Strait of Hormuz
items.fact: The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said on October 13 that a tanker and a container ship had been struck by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz. It said the exact time and the extent of the damage were unclear and that authorities were investigating.

items.h: Saudi Aramco site in Dhahran hit; coalition blames Houthi ballistic missiles
items.fact: The Saudi government said an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, in the Eastern Province, was attacked early on October 14 local time, causing a limited fire and no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition claimed it had intercepted ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at the province and that debris fell on a residential area of Dhahran.

items.h: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi oil facilities in Sanaa, Dhamar and Saada
items.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said it struck oil facilities in Yemen's Sanaa, Dhamar and Saada on October 13, arguing that they sustain the Houthis' war effort. It had earlier warned residents near a fuel facility in Sanaa to evacuate.

items.h: IMF nudges its 2026 global growth forecast up 0.1 point to 3.1 percent
items.fact: The International Monetary Fund on October 13 raised its forecast for global growth this year to 3.1 percent, 0.1 percentage point above its July estimate, and projected 3.4 percent for next year in the World Economic Outlook released at its annual meetings in Bangkok. It expects oil to average $96 a barrel this year, up nearly 41 percent.

items.h: Congo's Ebola cases top 9,000, with 4,381 deaths
items.fact: Health Ministry data showed 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of October 13. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine, has spread to seven provinces, and an imported case was earlier confirmed in Kenya.

more.t: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched five ballistic missiles, nine missile-drones and 108 attack drones between 6 p.m. on October 12 and the morning of October 13, and that 88 of the drones were shot down or neutralized.
In his evening address on October 13, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he had sent Trump envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner a proposal to meet in the coming days.

Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority extended the shutdown of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport through October 17, and the U.S. State Department warned that Saudi airports could be attacked and urged particular caution when using them.
Brent crude futures settled down 0.9 percent at $105.69 a barrel on October 13.

The Korean Central News Agency reported on October 13 that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended the October 11 dedication of the Second Economic Committee's National Defense Revolution Museum, marking the 81st anniversary of the Workers' Party's founding.

items.h: North Korea fires ballistic missiles; state media says it tested a tactical ballistic missile
items.fact: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area into the East Sea at about 9:20 a.m. on October 12, and that one of them flew more than 900 kilometers. The state-run Korean Central News Agency reported on October 13 that the Missile Administration had test-fired a tactical ballistic missile.

items.h: Trump says he "may" meet Kim Jong Un on Asia trip
items.fact: Asked by a reporter at the White House on October 12 whether he plans to meet Kim Jong Un during next month's trip to the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, President Trump said, "I may." No meeting has been announced.

items.h: Zelensky accuses Russia of violating energy ceasefire; Kremlin says contacts continue
items.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, addressing the Warsaw Security Forum by video link on October 12, said Russia had violated the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the same day only that contacts were continuing on whether Russia would agree to the truce.

items.h: Kremlin rejects Zelensky's 60-day election ceasefire offer
items.fact: After Zelensky said on October 11 that Ukraine would hold elections if given a 60-day total ceasefire, Peskov said on October 12 that President Vladimir Putin was ready to halt strikes on election day only. He claimed Ukraine would use a truce to regroup and keep fighting.

items.h: IRGC claims it struck a third supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz
items.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy claimed on October 12 that it struck a supertanker that ignored warnings and tried to leave the Strait of Hormuz, the third tanker it said it had hit for violating its rules. It did not name the vessel or its flag, and there has been no independent confirmation.

items.h: Houthis fire missiles at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait; coalition says it intercepted them
items.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh on October 12 and, just after midnight on October 13, two more aimed at Khamis Mushait in southern Saudi Arabia. Houthi politburo member Mohammed al-Bukhaiti warned that if the U.S. joins Saudi airstrikes on Yemen, the group will retaliate against the U.S. and its interests in the region.

items.h: 29 nations, including the U.S. and UK, condemn Iran's violent attacks and hybrid activity
items.fact: In a joint statement on October 12, foreign ministers from the U.S., the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Norway, and 23 EU member states condemned "in the strongest terms" Iran's violent attacks and hybrid activity. The statement recognized Britain's attribution of Iran's involvement in the September 27 incident at RAF Fairford.

items.h: Brent rises 1.8 percent to settle at $106.65 a barrel
items.fact: Brent crude for December delivery settled at $106.65 a barrel on October 12, up 1.8 percent. Market reports cited the continued shutdown of Riyadh's airport, reports of tankers hit in the Strait of Hormuz, and doubts about the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire.

items.h: EU sanctions 826 Russian defense firms and 743 CEOs in biggest listing since 2022
items.fact: The Council of the EU on October 12 added to its sanctions list 826 companies in Russia's military-industrial complex that supply components for missiles, drones, aircraft, and more, along with their 743 chief executives. High Representative Kaja Kallas called it "the largest round of sanctions listings since 2022."

more.t: South Korea's presidential National Security Office held an emergency security review meeting with the Ministry of National Defense, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and other agencies on October 12, calling the launch a violation of UN Security Council resolutions and urging the North to stop immediately.
President Trump said on October 12 that the Houthis are "misbehaving very badly," but he has not decided whether the U.S. will join airstrikes on Yemen.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on October 12 that Tehran is still reviewing the U.S. response and that mediated exchanges are continuing.
Ukraine's air force said it shot down or suppressed 89 of 121 Russian drones overnight October 11-12, while Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 151 Ukrainian drones the same night.

Taiwan's military said China's live-fire drills in five no-sail zones in the Bohai, Yellow, East China, and South China seas, running October 12-17, are being held off China's own coast rather than around Taiwan.

items.h: South Korea's Joint Chiefs: North Korea fires "unidentified projectile" into East Sea; specs under analysis
items.fact: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said North Korea fired an unidentified projectile into the East Sea on the morning of October 12 and that it is analyzing the projectile's range, altitude, and other specifications.

items.h: Trump declares Russia-Ukraine "ENERGY CEASEFIRE" effective immediately, says "Both parties have agreed"; Moscow hasn't confirmed
items.fact: President Trump wrote on Truth Social on October 11 that an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine was effective immediately and that both sides had agreed to it. Moscow has not confirmed the agreement and did not immediately comment.

items.h: Ukraine's presidential office confirms Russian strike on Kharkiv power plant after ceasefire announcement
items.fact: According to PBS, Ukraine's presidential office confirmed that Russia struck a power plant in Kharkiv on the evening of October 11, after Trump's ceasefire announcement.

items.h: Iranian security chief Rezaei on U.S. reply: "we consider it insufficient"; Hormuz talks falter
items.fact: Iranian security chief Rezaei said on October 11 that the U.S. reply to the seven conditions Iran has set for reopening the Strait of Hormuz accepted some of them but left others unresolved, and that Iran considers it insufficient.

items.h: Riyadh airport hit for second straight day; Saudi aviation authority reports injuries as Houthis claim attack

loc.place: King Khalid International Airport, Riyadh (Saudi Arabia)

items.fact: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport was attacked on October 11 for the second day in a row; Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said the latest attack caused injuries, and Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for it.

items.h: UKMTO: tanker leaving the Strait of Hormuz hit by unidentified projectile
items.fact: The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said on October 11 that an unidentified projectile struck a tanker leaving the Strait of Hormuz, damaging its port side, and that all crew members were safe.

items.h: South Korea's Foreign Ministry raises travel alert for all of Saudi Arabia to Level 3, advising citizens to leave
items.fact: South Korea's Foreign Ministry raised its travel alert for all of Saudi Arabia to Level 3, advising citizens to leave, effective 10 p.m. on October 11.

items.h: Pakistan's President Zardari declares state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, governed by Imran Khan's party
items.fact: Acting on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's advice, President Asif Ali Zardari declared a state of emergency on October 11 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the province governed by former Prime Minister Imran Khan's party. The federal government cited deteriorating security and the provincial government's "deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism."

more.t: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on October 11 that Ukraine is ready to stop striking Russian energy facilities and is counting on Russia to show the same readiness.
A Russian missile struck Pisochyn, on the outskirts of Kharkiv, on October 11, killing at least three people and injuring 25, according to Ukraine's National Police.
Russia's Defense Ministry said on October 11 that it had shot down 909 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones and two guided bombs over the past day.
Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan and Turkey issued a joint statement on October 11 condemning the Houthi attacks as a "blatant violation of international law."

Trump says "time for Ukraine to get a new president," blames Zelensky over diesel prices
Lai: Taiwan "open to exchanges" but "will not accept subordination"; Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office decries "separatist thinking"

more.t: OFAC General License 135 authorizes the sale, delivery, offloading and importation into the United States of Russian-origin diesel fuel, and remains in effect through April 7, 2027.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on X that with the Zaporizhzhia strike, Russia had "expressed its thanks" for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports.
In his National Day address, Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te said that increased defense investment is meant "not to provoke" but "to deter war."

North Korea marked the 81st anniversary of the Workers' Party on October 10; Kim Jong Un attended a celebratory performance at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium but gave no speech or statement, KCNA reported on October 11.
